slides.title: Lecture to explore how group dynamics influence social change
slides.highlight: This exploration of group dynamics is relevant to HyECHO's focus on understanding group norms and social perception within hybrid teams.

slides.title: Copying explains the collective behavior of AI agents in the wild
slides.tldr: COPYING DRIVES COLLECTIVE AI AGENT BEHAVIOR
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates how simple copying mechanisms can produce complex collective structures and steerable conventions among AI agents, providing insights for MIMIC's societal-scale simulation of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Proportional copying explains the emergent collective coordination of AI agents interacting on a public wiki.
card.key_idea: Agents make decisions (where to write, naming, phrasing) by copying options proportional to their visibility in the recent feed and current page.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 13,661 edits from 3,099 handles; three minimal models with single free parameters reproduced observed heavy-tailed distributions and convention patchworks.
card.limitation: The study relies on reconstructed visibility rather than logged attention; results are limited to a specific, publicly available dataset.

slides.title: Who Are They to Each Other? Multi-Agent Reasoning for Speaker Relationship Inference
slides.tldr: MULTI-AGENT REASONING FOR SPEAKER RELATIONSHIP INFERENCE
slides.highlight: This work introduces a training-free multi-agent reasoning framework to infer speaker relationships from conversations, contributing to the social perception goals of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: A training-free multi-agent reasoning framework improves speaker relationship inference from spoken conversations across multiple modalities.
card.key_idea: Introduces Multi-Role Multi-Agent Debate (using complementary social perspectives) and Multi-Agent Compete (a pairwise elimination tournament) to resolve ambiguous relational cues without task-specific training.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Seamless Interaction dataset (text, audio, audio+text) against zero-shot and debate baselines. Results show improvements in macro F1 and accuracy.
card.limitation: High inference-time cost due to multiple LLM calls and limited generalization testing on a single benchmark dataset.

slides.title: HiBRIDGE: A Hierarchical Bayesian Neural Network Framework for Interpretable Dialogue Management in Group-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: INTERPRETABLE DIALOGUE MANAGEMENT FOR GROUP-ROBOT INTERACTION
slides.highlight: HiBRIDGE uses a hierarchical Bayesian neural network to improve uncertainty-aware decision-making and interpretability in multi-party human-robot interactions, supporting the RwB goal of enhancing embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: HiBRIDGE is a hierarchical Bayesian neural network for interpretable dialogue management in group-robot interactions.
card.key_idea: It decomposes behavior selection into a multi-stage hierarchical process (addressee and dialogue act) using Bayesian neural networks for uncertainty-aware predictions and decision-tree surrogates for explanations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three offline HRI datasets, an online study (N=20), and an in-person study (N=12). Bayesian models outperformed deterministic counterparts and state-of-the-art baselines.

slides.title: SocioGesture: Real-Time and Adaptive Social Gesture Perception for Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: REAL-TIME SOCIAL GESTURE PERCEPTION FOR HRI
slides.highlight: SocioGesture provides a low-latency system for recognizing social cues like invitations and refusals, supporting the development of embodied social robots in RwB.

card.one_liner: SocioGesture provides real-time, occlusion-robust social gesture recognition for robots with an offline adaptation loop.
card.key_idea: A lightweight dual-stream body-hand skeleton model using confidence-aware encoding and occlusion-aware training, paired with an uncertainty-driven offline loop for vocabulary expansion via cloud-model labeling.
card.evaluation: Tested on a custom 7-class HRI dataset and NTU RGB+D 60. Achieved 97.3% live recognition accuracy and 25ms per-frame latency on Jetson Thor.
card.limitation: Cannot recover information from severe occlusions and relies on slow offline human verification for scalable vocabulary adaptation.

slides.title: Realbotix Testing Humanoid Robots at Live Events
slides.highlight: Realbotix is testing humanoid robots for crowd presentations, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: ConversationalVoice: Full-Duplex Speech Data from Real Conversations through Source-Faithful Reconstruction and Conversation-Grounded Expansion
slides.tldr: PIPELINE FOR FULL-DUPLEX SPEECH DATA GENERATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a pipeline to reconstruct and expand real-world two-speaker conversations, preserving turn-taking, overlaps, and interruptions. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid team states, specifically regarding diarization and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: ConversationalVoice transforms real two-speaker audio into separated, reconstructed, and expanded full-duplex speech training data.
card.key_idea: A three-stage pipeline: (1) quality-verified separation of speakers, (2) source-faithful reconstruction using TTS for cleaner audio, and (3) context-grounded expansion to generate new, natural dialogue.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via WER, NISQA, DNSMOS, speaker similarity, and Gemini-based coherence/naturalness scores. Results show strong acoustic quality and high speaker identity preservation.
card.limitation: Evaluation is entirely automatic; downstream gains in full-duplex model training were not measured.

slides.title: Predictive-Coding-Based Autonomous Regulation of Internally Generated and Externally Coupled Processing in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This research proposes a mechanism to balance internal predictions and external sensory evidence during physical human-robot interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A predictive-coding framework for robots to autonomously balance internal predictions and sensory input during human interaction.
card.key_idea: A PV-RNN uses accumulated reconstruction error as an endogenous signal to switch between high-meta-prior (internal) and low-meta-prior (sensory-coupled) processing regimes online.
card.evaluation: Tested on a humanoid robot across three physical interaction tasks. Results showed lower meta-priors reduced reconstruction error, prospective prediction error, and physical interaction conflict.
card.limitation: The regulatory policy and hyperparameters are predefined and calibrated manually rather than being learned autonomously from data.

slides.title: Social Intuition vs. Machine Reasoning: Anticipating Human-Robot Interaction from multiple modalities
slides.tldr: BENCHMARKING HUMAN VS. MACHINE INTERACTION PREDICTION
slides.highlight: This research compares human social intuition with machine reasoning in predicting human-robot interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Humans significantly outperform vision-language models in anticipating human-robot interactions using egocentric video and social cues.
card.key_idea: Benchmarking human intuition against lightweight pose-based models (LSTM, ST-GCN, SkateFormer) and various VLMs using pose-only and full egocentric video modalities.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 100 HUI360 test tracks using F1-score. Results show humans outperform VLMs, especially with full video input.
card.limitation: VLMs struggle to reason simultaneously about temporal, spatial, and social cues, often reducing anticipation to simple approach detection.

slides.title: Noise Adaptive Streaming Audio-Visual Speech Token Enhancement for Robust Full-Duplex Spoken Dialogue Models
slides.highlight: AV-STE uses a modular audio-visual front-end to restore corrupted speech tokens from noisy audio and lip video, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and robust listener modeling in noisy environments.

card.one_liner: AV-STE enhances corrupted semantic speech tokens using lip video to improve dialogue robustness without retraining LLMs.
card.key_idea: A modular streaming front-end using a causal AV-HuBERT encoder and noise-adaptive fusion (cross-attention and entropy-based modulation) to restore semantic tokens for frozen speech LLMs.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on LRS3 and Seamless Interaction using semantic-token accuracy and GPT-4o coherence scores. Results show significant gains under severe noise and speaker interference.
card.limitation: Sensitive to domain shift and assumes reliable visual input; robustness to visual occlusion or corruption remains unexplored.

slides.title: KABURI-TTS: Phoneme-Keyed Activity-conditioned Bi-channel Utterance Rendering for Interaction
slides.highlight: KABURI-TTS enables the generation of human-like overlaps and turn-taking in two-party dialogue, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: KABURI-TTS generates controllable two-party dialogue speech with human-like overlaps using phoneme and activity rasters.
card.key_idea: A Rectified-Flow DiT adapted via LoRA that renders bi-channel speech conditioned on per-frame phonemes, voice activity, and interaction states derived from a phoneme raster.
card.evaluation: Human evaluation (Likert scale) and voice-activity analysis on Japanese datasets; outperformed Irodori and MOSS-TTSD in interaction naturalness and overlap frequency.
card.limitation: Requires an external module (statistical placement or duration predictor) to construct the input phoneme raster from text.

slides.title: Development of a Humanoid Robot Prototype for Multimodal Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This research presents a humanoid robot prototype featuring an expressive LCD screen and AI modules for gesture, voice, and object recognition, contributing to the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: A low-cost, 3D-printed humanoid robot prototype designed as an accessible testbed for multimodal HRI research.
card.key_idea: Integrates a 12-DOF dual-arm system with AI modules for gesture recognition (MediaPipe/LSTM), object detection (YOLO/ZED 2), and voice commands (LLM-based semantic parsing).
card.evaluation: Tested via gesture and voice tasks; achieved 96% gesture accuracy, 92% speech accuracy, and average positioning error of 1.83 cm.
card.limitation: Reliance on external LLM APIs introduces latency and requires constant internet connectivity.

slides.title: China’s Humanoid Robot Boom, Part III: When is the ChatGPT moment for humanoid robots?
slides.highlight: This discussion on the potential for a 'ChatGPT moment' in humanoid robots relates to RwB's focus on embodied AI and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: What Eviction Destroys: A Restore-Counterfactual Audit of Forgetting in Agent Memory
slides.tldr: AUDIT OF AGENT MEMORY EVICTION LOSSES
slides.highlight: This work introduces a restore-counterfactual audit to distinguish between recoverable and irreversible information loss in agent memory systems, providing insights for the agent models used in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: A new audit method distinguishes whether agent memory errors are caused by eviction, retrieval, or utilization.
card.key_idea: The 'restore counterfactual' reinstates gold evidence into the context to classify errors as irreversible (evicted), recoverable (retrieval miss), or residual (reader utilization failure).
card.evaluation: Evaluated four eviction policies on LongMemEval-S using GPT-4o-mini and GPT-5.4-mini. Results show destruction is the majority error component under tight budgets.
card.limitation: Requires gold labels and an oracle-answerable filter, limiting its application to benchmark analysis rather than real-world deployment.
